title: Business & Economic English: The Economist Style & Harvard Business Review Analytical Framework
evaluation: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5) — Gold Standard for Corporate & Macroeconomic English

economist_style_commandments.commandment: 1. Never use a metaphor, simile, or other figure of speech which you are used to seeing in print.
economist_style_commandments.rationale: Clichés dull the mind and conceal lack of original thought.

economist_style_commandments.commandment: 2. Never use a long word where a short one will do.
economist_style_commandments.rationale: Clarity is power. Prefer 'use' over 'utilize', 'end' over 'terminate'.

economist_style_commandments.commandment: 3. If it is possible to cut a word out, always cut it out.
economist_style_commandments.rationale: Economic prose must be muscular and lean.

economist_style_commandments.commandment: 4. Never use the passive where you can use the active.
economist_style_commandments.rationale: Active verbs identify accountability and establish causality.

economist_style_commandments.commandment: 5. Never use a foreign phrase, scientific word, or jargon if you can think of an everyday English equivalent.

macroeconomic_lexicon_for_ielts_and_exec.definition: Government policies to reduce budget deficits through spending cuts or tax hikes.
Congestion points that impede the smooth flow of goods from manufacture to retail.
Factors causing rising price levels across a national economy.
The degree to which a product or service is adopted by target consumers.
Legal and governmental compliance constraints that hinder corporate expansion.
Innovations that fundamentally alter how an entire industry operates.

hbr_case_study_analytical_template.section_1_executive_summary: Concise 3-sentence synthesis stating the core strategic dilemma, the root cause, and the recommended intervention.
hbr_case_study_analytical_template.section_2_strategic_diagnosis: Evaluating competitive positioning, macroeconomic constraints, and internal operational bottlenecks.
hbr_case_study_analytical_template.section_3_alternative_options: Contrasting two mutually exclusive courses of action with explicit risk-benefit trade-offs.
hbr_case_study_analytical_template.section_4_implementation_roadmap: Milestone scheduling, resource allocation, and key performance indicators (KPIs).
